import Mathlib

inductive Color
| Red
| Black
deriving Inhabited, BEq

inductive Node
| Empty : Node
| Tree  (color : Color) (val : Int) (left : Node) (right : Node) : Node
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : Node) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => ∅
  | Node.Tree _ v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_red (t : Node) : Bool :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree Color.Red _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false

def get_color (t : Node) : Color :=
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c _ _ _ => c
  | Node.Empty => Color.Black -- Empty nodes are black

def is_bst (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => True
  | Node.Tree _ v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

-- Black Height: Returns -1 if invalid
def black_height (t : Node) : Int :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => 1
  | Node.Tree c _ l r =>
    let lh := black_height l
    let rh := black_height r
    if lh ≠ -1 ∧ rh ≠ -1 ∧ lh = rh then
      if c == Color.Black then lh + 1 else lh
    else
      -1

def satisfies_red_props (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => True
  | Node.Tree _ _ l r =>
    satisfies_red_props l ∧
    satisfies_red_props r ∧
    -- Rule: No Right-Leaning Red
    (¬ is_red r) ∧
    -- Rule: No Double Red on Left
    (match l with
     | Node.Tree Color.Red _ ll _ => ¬ is_red ll
     | _ => True)

-- Main Invariant
def is_llrbt (t : Node) : Prop :=
  is_bst t ∧
  black_height t ≠ -1 ∧
  satisfies_red_props t

def get_left (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ l _ => some l | _ => none

def get_right (t : Node) : Option Node :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ _ _ r => some r | _ => none

def get_val (t : Node) : Option Int :=
  match t with | Node.Tree _ v _ _ => some v | _ => none

def is_not_empty (t : Node) : Prop :=
  match t with | Node.Empty => False | _ => True

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def flip_colors_precond (t : Node) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  -- t is not empty
  is_not_empty t ∧
  is_bst t ∧
  match t with
  | Node.Tree c _ l r =>
    is_not_empty l ∧ is_not_empty r ∧
    (get_color l = get_color r) ∧
    (c ≠ get_color l)
  | _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- Invert a single color
def flip_color (c : Color) : Color :=
  match c with
  | Color.Red => Color.Black
  | Color.Black => Color.Red

-- Recolor the root of a tree, keeping value and subtrees untouched
def set_color (c : Color) (t : Node) : Node :=
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => Node.Empty
  | Node.Tree _ v l r => Node.Tree c v l r
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def flip_colors (t : Node) 
    (h_precond : flip_colors_precond t) : Node :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match t with
  | Node.Empty => Node.Empty
  | Node.Tree c v l r =>
      Node.Tree (flip_color c) v
        (set_color (flip_color (get_color l)) l)
        (set_color (flip_color (get_color r)) r)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def flip_colors_postcond (t : Node) (result : Node)
    (_ : flip_colors_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  view result = view t ∧
  is_bst result ∧ -- Requirement 1: BST structure preserved
  black_height result = black_height t ∧ -- Requirement 2: Balance preserved (Critical)
  match result, t with
  | Node.Tree c' _ l' r', Node.Tree c _ l r =>
      c' ≠ c ∧
      get_color l' ≠ get_color l ∧
      get_color r' ≠ get_color r
  | _, _ => False
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- Decidable equality facts for the derived BEq instance on Color
theorem beq_black_black : (Color.Black == Color.Black) = true := rfl

theorem beq_red_black : (Color.Red == Color.Black) = false := rfl

-- Clean unfolding lemmas for black_height at each color
theorem bh_black (v : Int) (l r : Node) :
    black_height (Node.Tree Color.Black v l r) =
      if black_height l ≠ -1 ∧ black_height r ≠ -1 ∧ black_height l = black_height r
      then black_height l + 1 else -1 := by
  rw [black_height]
  simp [beq_black_black]

theorem bh_red (v : Int) (l r : Node) :
    black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red v l r) =
      if black_height l ≠ -1 ∧ black_height r ≠ -1 ∧ black_height l = black_height r
      then black_height l else -1 := by
  rw [black_height]
  simp [beq_red_black]

-- A black height is either the error marker -1 or at least 1
theorem black_height_cases (t : Node) : black_height t = -1 ∨ 1 ≤ black_height t := by
  induction t with
  | Empty => right; simp [black_height]
  | Tree c v l r ihl ihr =>
      cases c
      · rw [bh_red]; split_ifs <;> omega
      · rw [bh_black]; split_ifs <;> omega

-- The core balance fact: pushing the redness one level down (or up) keeps the
-- black height of the cluster unchanged, error marker included.
theorem bh_flip (v vl vr : Int) (ll lr rl rr : Node) :
    black_height (Node.Tree Color.Red v (Node.Tree Color.Black vl ll lr)
        (Node.Tree Color.Black vr rl rr))
      = black_height (Node.Tree Color.Black v (Node.Tree Color.Red vl ll lr)
        (Node.Tree Color.Red vr rl rr)) := by
  have h1 := black_height_cases ll
  have h2 := black_height_cases lr
  have h3 := black_height_cases rl
  have h4 := black_height_cases rr
  simp only [bh_black, bh_red]
  split_ifs <;> omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem flip_colors_postcond_satisfied (t : Node)
    (h_precond : flip_colors_precond t) :
    flip_colors_postcond t (flip_colors t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  cases t with
  | Empty => simp [is_not_empty] at h_precond
  | Tree c v l r =>
      have hp := h_precond
      obtain ⟨-, hbst, hlne, hrne, hcc, hcne⟩ := hp
      cases l with
      | Empty => simp [is_not_empty] at hlne
      | Tree cl vl ll lr =>
          cases r with
          | Empty => simp [is_not_empty] at hrne
          | Tree cr vr rl rr =>
              have hcc' : cl = cr := by simpa [get_color] using hcc
              have hcne' : c ≠ cl := by simpa [get_color] using hcne
              cases c <;> cases cl <;> cases cr
              case Red.Red.Red => exact absurd rfl hcne'
              case Red.Red.Black => exact absurd hcc' (by simp)
              case Red.Black.Red => exact absurd hcc' (by simp)
              case Black.Red.Black => exact absurd hcc' (by simp)
              case Black.Black.Red => exact absurd hcc' (by simp)
              case Black.Black.Black => exact absurd rfl hcne'
              -- Valid case 1: red root, black children -> black root, red children
              case Red.Black.Black =>
                  have hres : flip_colors _ h_precond
                      = Node.Tree Color.Black v (Node.Tree Color.Red vl ll lr)
                          (Node.Tree Color.Red vr rl rr) := rfl
                  rw [hres]
                  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
                  · simp only [view]
                  · simp only [is_bst, view] at hbst ⊢
                    exact hbst
                  · exact (bh_flip v vl vr ll lr rl rr).symm
                  · simp
                  · simp [get_color]
                  · simp [get_color]
              -- Valid case 2: black root, red children -> red root, black children
              case Black.Red.Red =>
                  have hres : flip_colors _ h_precond
                      = Node.Tree Color.Red v (Node.Tree Color.Black vl ll lr)
                          (Node.Tree Color.Black vr rl rr) := rfl
                  rw [hres]
                  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
                  · simp only [view]
                  · simp only [is_bst, view] at hbst ⊢
                    exact hbst
                  · exact bh_flip v vl vr ll lr rl rr
                  · simp
                  · simp [get_color]
                  · simp [get_color]
  -- !benchmark @end proof

**LEAN VERIFIED** — final run confirms it, and the earlier failure cause (`sorry` in the `code` section) is gone.

## What I changed

The preserved `Solution.lean` was byte-identical to the scaffold (both `sorry`s still present), so all four editable regions needed real content. Only `auxcode`, `code`, `lemma`, and `proof` were touched.

- **auxcode**: `flip_color` (color inversion) and `set_color` (recolor a root, preserving value and subtrees).
- **code**: `flip_colors` inverts the root color and the root color of each child.
- **lemma**: two `rfl` facts for the derived `BEq Color`; `bh_black` / `bh_red` clean unfoldings of `black_height`; `black_height_cases` (`bh t = -1 ∨ 1 ≤ bh t`, by induction); and `bh_flip`, the core balance fact that moving redness one level down/up leaves the cluster's black height identical.
- **proof**: case analysis on the tree and both children (`Empty` cases discharged from the `is_not_empty` preconditions), then all 8 root/child color combinations — 6 contradict `get_color l = get_color r` or `c ≠ get_color l`, and the 2 legal ones (Red root/Black children, Black root/Red children) are proven in full.

## Semantic audit vs TASK.md

- **Preconditions** (teacher-owned, unedited): non-empty node, non-empty children, equal child colors, root color differing from children — every one is *used* to discharge cases, none assumed away or weakened.
- **Postconditions**: all four conjuncts proven genuinely — `view result = view t`, `is_bst result` (derived from `is_bst t`, not asserted), `black_height result = black_height t`, and all three colors strictly inverted.
- **Black height** is the substantive part: `bh_flip` covers the `-1` error marker on both sides, so the equality holds even though the precondition does *not* require `black_height t ≠ -1`. `black_height_cases` supplies the `bh ≥ 1` fact needed to rule out `bh + 1 = -1`.
- **No placeholders**: no `:= 0`, `:= True`, or trivially-true helper; each lemma is a real statement with a real proof.
- **Adversarial inputs**: values are `Int` and universally quantified in `bh_flip`; nothing in the function or proof depends on value sign or magnitude, so all-negative (or mixed) trees behave identically. Empty children are excluded by precondition, and `flip_colors`' `Empty` branch is total but unreachable.

One thing worth flagging (not fixable by me): TASK.md mentions invariant maintenance "using `is_llrbt`", but the teacher-owned `postcond` region only demands `is_bst` + `black_height`, not `satisfies_red_props`. That's the correct specification — a local color flip genuinely can create a right-leaning red as seen from the parent — so the weaker conjunct is intended, not something I relaxed.

analysis:
The implementation performs the required LLRBT color flip directly:

- It pattern-matches on the root.
- It inverts the root color with `flip_color`.
- It inverts each child’s root color using `set_color`.
- It leaves all values, child subtrees, and tree structure unchanged.

Thus, for the two valid configurations, it maps:

- Black root with Red children → Red root with Black children.
- Red root with Black children → Black root with Red children.

The proof establishes preservation of the represented set, BST ordering, and black height, as well as inversion of all three relevant colors. The auxiliary `bh_flip` lemma proves the local black-height preservation from the recursive definition rather than relying on an external verified implementation.

There are no apparent verification cheats: no `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, empty proof placeholders, or calls to a preexisting color-flip implementation. Although the impossible `Node.Empty` branch returns `Empty`, that branch is unreachable under the supplied precondition and is normal for a total Lean definition.

The natural-language description mentions `is_llrbt`, while the stated postcondition separately checks BST and black-height preservation rather than asserting the full predicate. Under the instruction to accept the teacher-provided specification and not challenge it, this is not a defect in the student’s implementation. The algorithm itself is the standard local `flip_colors` operation.
